title: Thrift Store Thrills: Creative DIY Halloween Costumes on a Budget
text:
Halloween costs can skyrocket, but thrift stores offer an affordable and eco-friendly alternative for creating unique DIY costumes. By selecting items that spark inspiration or targeting specific pieces, families can save money, reduce landfill waste from fast fashion, and make the holiday more memorable through creativity.
— For most people these days, Halloween means buying a costume from a website or a specialty Halloween store, and those costumes can cost up to $50 or more.
On top of that, some families are buying costumes for multiple children. Halloween prices don't need to be so scary, and a thrift store is the perfect place to save money, be creative and keep fast-fashion costumes out of our landfills. In my opinion, there are two ways to go about it.
First, you can start with knowing exactly what you want to be and go searching. One year, I knew I wanted to be a ghost. So, I went to the thrift store and bought a bunch of white clothing and white fabric. I ripped it and tied it and painted my face.
Here is how it turned out: It can even be something simple. One year, I knew I wanted to be a ragdoll. So, I bought two sweaters, cut them in half, and used some twine to make them look like they were sewn back up together. You may remember last year, I was Alexander Hamilton live on the air on Halloween Night.
I knew I wanted to be him when I went to the thrift store. So, I bought a blue blazer, I bought khaki pants, and I got lace curtains for the neck piece. The other option for thrifting is letting the store tell you what your costume will be.
For example, I found a yellow pants suit and used it to be The Mask. One year, I found a red jacket at the thrift store that reminded me of Michael Jackson, so I thrifted some black pants and added gold details to the outfit. Lastly, you can use things you already have. Look in your closet — what inspires you?
I put on white clothes I already had and a bald cap to be Mr. Clean. Halloween can be a fun time to get creative. Let kids be proud of the costume they helped make. One trip to the thrift store could save you money and help make new memories this Halloween.
